candidates.title: A multi-task learning-based network for detecting three-dimensional osteometric landmarks of the shoulder joint
candidates.abstract: Background Mirror-based preoperative planning for total shoulder arthroplasty relies on accurate three-dimensional (3D) localization of bony landmarks on the contralateral, anatomically intact shoulder. Manual annotation is time-consuming and shows inter- and intra-observer variability. The aim of this study was to develop and evaluate a multi-task deep-learning network for automated 3D bony landmark detection on contralateral shoulder CT. Methods In this single-center retrospective study, 179 patients with intact contralateral shoulder CT scans were split at the patient level into training (n = 125), validation (n = 18), and test (n = 36) sets. We developed a dual-decoder 3D BiFormer-UNet for humerus and scapula segmentation and heatmap-based localization of 14 anatomical landmarks. A cross-task feature-fusion (CtFF) module transferred bone-structural guidance from the segmentation decoder to the landmark decoder. The network was trained end-to-end using a composite loss comprising hard-negative-mining heatmap regression, a geometric structure constraint, distance-aware similarity learning, and auxiliary segmentation loss. Landmark localization was evaluated using MRE and SDR at thresholds of 2.0, 2.5, 3.0, and 4.0 mm, while segmentation was assessed using the Dice coefficient. Per-case MRE was compared with four 3D baseline models using paired tests with Holm–Bonferroni correction. Results In the 36-case test set, the proposed model achieved an MRE of 2.1 ± 1.2 mm (95% CI, 1.7–2.5 mm) and SDRs of 72.0%, 81.8%, 90.3%, and 96.7% at thresholds of 2.0, 2.5, 3.0, and 4.0 mm, respectively. Its MRE was significantly lower than those of 3D U-Net, V-Net, 3D HRNet adaptation, and H3DE-Net (all Holm–Bonferroni-adjusted P < 0.05). On the test set, the auxiliary segmentation branch achieved mean Dice coefficients of 0.83 ± 0.05 for the humerus and 0.78 ± 0.07 for the scapula. Internally defined center landmarks, particularly the humeral head rotation center, anatomical neck center, and proximal and distal medullary canal centers, showed larger localization errors (2.3–2.6 mm) than most surface landmarks. Conclusion The proposed multi-task framework demonstrated promising 3D landmark localization performance on intact contralateral shoulder CT by integrating global anatomical context with bone-structural guidance. It may serve as an upstream localization component for mirror-based shoulder arthroplasty planning, although external validation is required before clinical use.

candidates.title: Interpretable and backpropagation-free Green Learning for efficient multi-task echocardiographic segmentation and classification
candidates.abstract: Purpose This study develops an interpretable, backpropagation-free multi-task Green Learning (MTGL) framework for automated echocardiographic analysis. It addresses the need for reliable left ventricular (LV) segmentation and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) classification while reducing the parameter burden, energy demand and opacity associated with conventional deep learning (DL) models. The objective is to determine whether a unified feed-forward framework can deliver clinically relevant accuracy, computational efficiency and interpretable feature representations. Design/methodology/approach The framework uses a four-hop, PCA/Saab-based unsupervised VoxelHop encoder followed by a coarse-to-fine XGBoost residual-regression decoder for LV segmentation and a pooled multi-scale XGBoost classifier for three-class LVEF classification. Experiments used the predefined EchoNet-Dynamic training, validation and test partitions. MTGL was evaluated against matched 3D V-Net, 3D U-Net, 3D UNETR and 3D nnU-Net baselines using classification accuracy and balanced accuracy, and Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) and intersection over union (IoU). Findings On the EchoNet-Dynamic test set, MTGL achieved 94.3% accuracy for three-class LVEF classification, and 0.912 DSC for LV segmentation, outperforming all compared baselines. It used 1.13 million parameters, versus 10.47–49.08 million for the DL comparators, and showed the lowest measured training energy use and carbon emissions. Hop ablation further showed complementary multi-scale information, with the full feature set yielding the highest classification accuracy. Originality/value Unlike end-to-end backpropagation-based DL methods, MTGL combines an unsupervised linear VoxelHop representation with task-specific XGBoost decoders in a single multi-task echocardiographic pipeline. The PCA/Saab direct current and alternating current feature decomposition enables direct inspection of learned spatial and spatiotemporal signals, linking shallow features to anatomical boundaries and deeper features to global contractile dynamics. The study therefore demonstrates that a compact, interpretable Green Learning system can jointly support LV segmentation and LVEF grouping with strong in-domain performance and lower measured training environmental cost.

candidates.title: An explainable hybrid transformer–CNN framework for multi-class brain tumor classification from MRI images
candidates.abstract: Abstract The identification of brain tumors through magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) requires effective methods that provide precise results because these results determine clinical choices. The study presents a classification system based on hybrid Transformer-CNN technology which classifies brain tumors into multiple types by using tumor segmentation and deep feature extraction and explainable artificial intelligence. The preprocessing of MRI images involves several steps which include skull stripping and CLAHE-based contrast enhancement and normalization and data augmentation and resizing to create high-quality images that maintain uniformity for model input. The TransUNet architecture performs tumor region segmentation by integrating convolutional neural networks with transformer-based attention systems which enable it to recognize both nearby and distant contextual details. The system generates segmentation masks which enable region-of-interest (ROI) feature extraction through DenseNet121 that has been pretrained on ImageNet while the final classification layer gets removed and global average pooling produces discriminative feature representations. The system uses an attention-based feature refinement method to improve feature representation followed by a regularized fully connected deep classifier which includes batch normalization and dropout for four-class classification of tumors. Model interpretability is achieved using Grad-CAM++ and attention visualization, enabling clear identification of tumor-related regions and improving model transparency. Experimental evaluation demonstrates high classification performance, achieving accuracies of 98.54% for meningioma, 98.65% for glioma, 99.45% for pituitary tumors, and 99.56% for no-tumor cases. These results indicate that presented TransUNet–DenseNet121 approach offers an accurate, reliable, interpretable method for detection of brain tumors automatically from MRI scanned images.

candidates.title: Quantitative Measurement of White Matter Hyperintensities in Brain MRI using a Multimodal Boundary-Aware Dual-Task Segmentation Framework
candidates.abstract: White matter hyperintensity (WMH) subtype segmentation in brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) remains challenging due to heterogeneous lesion sizes, indistinct boundaries, and severe class imbalance. We propose a multimodal boundary-aware dual-task U-Net for segmenting periventricular (PVWMH), deep (DWMH), and subcortical (SWMH) lesions. The framework integrates FLAIR-T1-weighted feature fusion, Vision Mamba-based feature modeling, an SWMH-specific boundary loss, and auxiliary boundary detection. The method was evaluated using patient-level five-fold cross-validation on a private multicenter cohort (n = 75) and separately on 60 publicly annotated MICCAI WMH Challenge subjects for binary segmentation. On the private cohort, the proposed framework achieved an overall Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) of 0.6081 and a 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95) of 14.80 mm, compared with 0.5638 and 18.25 mm for the FLAIR-only ablation baseline. It also improved SWMH DSC from 0.4610 with nnU-Net to 0.5215 (p = 0.008). On the public dataset, the mean binary DSC and HD95 were 0.6812 and 12.91 mm, respectively.Given the relatively large through-plane voxel spacing (8.4 mm), the framework processes 2D axial slices independently and does not explicitly model inter-slice context, which may limit its ability to characterize lesions extending across adjacent slices.

candidates.title: Comparative Analysis and Adaptation Strategies of Vision Foundation Models in Dermoscopic Image Segmentation
candidates.abstract: Accurate segmentation of skin lesions is of critical clinical importance for early melanoma diagnosis; however, the direct application of large foundation models like the Segment Anything Model (SAM) to medical images characterized by low contrast and fuzzy boundaries remains insufficient due to substantial domain gaps. In current study, a parameter-efficient fine-tuning strategy is presented by integrating lightweight adapter modules into a frozen Vision Transformer backbone. The proposed SAM-Adapter approach was comparatively evaluated against the original SAM and MedSAM models on the publicly available ISIC2018 and HAM10000 dermoscopic datasets. Optimized with AdamW, the model achieved the highest Dice (0.9603) and IoU (0.9241) scores along with the lowest HD95 (22.57) value on the HAM10000 dataset. Validated as statistically significant via the Wilcoxon test, this approach minimized computational overhead while demonstrating superior accuracy in boundary delineation. This adapter-based framework is planned for integration into clinical decision-support systems and other medical imaging modalities.

candidates.title: Automated segmentation and quantification of histological liver features for MASH/MASLD scoring
candidates.abstract: Abstract The increasing global prevalence of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) including metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) creates an urgent need for objective histopathological assessment. Conventional histological approaches are time-consuming and subjective. Therefore, we propose a fully automated, deep-learning-based pipeline for the segmentation and characterisation of histological liver features of MASH/MASLD. Segmentation was applied to H&E sections from 45 mice and 44 humans with MASH/MASLD. Our qHisto (quantitative histology) method, is nnU-Net-based and quantifies key histological components of the MASH-score, including steatosis, fibrosis, inflammation and ballooning. Additionally, we determined novel features that are inaccessible through manual histology, like the distribution of fat droplet sizes, nuclear aspect ratio and heatmaps. qHisto parameters showed strong positive correlations with conventional histology scores (fat: R = 0.91, inflammation: R = 0.70, ballooning: R = 0.47) and with hepatic fat fraction by magnetic resonance imaging ( R = 0.87). Our novel scores showed that nuclei deformation is driven by large fat droplets rather than the overall amount of fat. A key advantage of our method is spatially resolved, precise histological quantification to provide detailed assessment of disease severity. By automating time-consuming and repetitive readouts, qHisto improves standardisation and reproducibility of MASH/MASLD feature quantification and provides scalable, slide-wide analysis that supports histopathologists and enhances clinical assessment.

candidates.title: Segment anything in medical images
candidates.abstract: Medical image segmentation is a critical component in clinical practice, facilitating accurate diagnosis, treatment planning, and disease monitoring. However, existing methods, often tailored to specific modalities or disease types, lack generalizability across the diverse spectrum of medical image segmentation tasks. Here we present MedSAM, a foundation model designed for bridging this gap by enabling universal medical image segmentation. The model is developed on a large-scale medical image dataset with 1,570,263 image-mask pairs, covering 10 imaging modalities and over 30 cancer types. We conduct a comprehensive evaluation on 86 internal validation tasks and 60 external validation tasks, demonstrating better accuracy and robustness than modality-wise specialist models. By delivering accurate and efficient segmentation across a wide spectrum of tasks, MedSAM holds significant potential to expedite the evolution of diagnostic tools and the personalization of treatment plans.

candidates.title: Additional file 1 of Medical Segment Anything Model (MedSAM): methodological innovations, evaluation practices, and clinical applications
MedSAM-U: Uncertainty-Guided Auto Multi-Prompt Adaptation for Reliable MedSAM
candidates.abstract: The Medical Segment Anything Model (MedSAM) has demonstrated strong performance in medical image segmentation, attracting increasing attention in the medical imaging domain. However, as with many prompt-based segmentation models, its performance is highly sensitive to the type and location of input prompts. This sensitivity often leads to suboptimal segmentation outcomes and necessitates labor-intensive manual prompt tuning, which hampers both efficiency and robustness. To address this challenge, this paper proposes MedSAM-U, an uncertainty-guided framework designed to automatically refine prompt inputs and enhance segmentation reliability. Specifically, a Multi-Prompt Adapter is integrated into MedSAM, resulting in MPA-MedSAM, which enables the model to effectively accommodate diverse multi-prompt inputs. An uncertainty estimation module is then introduced to evaluate the reliability of the prompts and their initial segmentation results. Based on this, a novel uncertainty-guided prompt adaptation strategy is applied to automatically generate refined prompts and more accurate segmentation outputs. The proposed MedSAM-U framework is evaluated across multiple medical imaging modalities. Experimental results on five diverse datasets demonstrate that MedSAM-U achieves consistent performance improvements ranging from 1.7% to 20.5% over the baseline MedSAM, confirming its effectiveness and practicality for robust and efficient medical image segmentation.

candidates.title: Evaluating a Deep Learning Foundation Model for Neuroimaging Segmentation in the Data-Rich and Data-Constrained Settings
candidates.abstract: Motivation: Deep learning models for segmentation require large datasets, limiting their use in clinical settings. Foundation models, which learn from non-medical images before fine-tuning for specific tasks, have emerged as a possible solution. Goal(s): We aimed to adapt and evaluate a recent foundation model, the Medical Segment Anything model (MedSAM), for neuroanatomy segmentation. Approach: Using the Human Connectome Project dataset, we trained MedSAM to segment 102 regions-of-interest and compared its accuracy with a baseline UNet model. Results: UNet outperformed MedSAM in almost all regions and dataset sizes, but MedSAM showed potential when training with very few MRIs. Impact: While foundation models such as MedSAM have potential for medical segmentation, they currently may not surpass traditional models when using sufficient data. In the data-limited setting, however, they can be useful when extremely little labeled data is available.

candidates.title: Development and validation of an autonomous artificial intelligence agent for clinical decision-making in oncology
candidates.abstract: Clinical decision-making in oncology is complex, requiring the integration of multimodal data and multidomain expertise. We developed and evaluated an autonomous clinical artificial intelligence (AI) agent leveraging GPT-4 with multimodal precision oncology tools to support personalized clinical decision-making. The system incorporates vision transformers for detecting microsatellite instability and KRAS and BRAF mutations from histopathology slides, MedSAM for radiological image segmentation and web-based search tools such as OncoKB, PubMed and Google. Evaluated on 20 realistic multimodal patient cases, the AI agent autonomously used appropriate tools with 87.5% accuracy, reached correct clinical conclusions in 91.0% of cases and accurately cited relevant oncology guidelines 75.5% of the time. Compared to GPT-4 alone, the integrated AI agent drastically improved decision-making accuracy from 30.3% to 87.2%. These findings demonstrate that integrating language models with precision oncology and search tools substantially enhances clinical accuracy, establishing a robust foundation for deploying AI-driven personalized oncology support systems.

candidates.title: Point-supervised Brain Tumor Segmentation with Box-prompted MedSAM
candidates.abstract: Delineating lesions and anatomical structure is important for image-guided interventions. Point-supervised medical image segmentation (PSS) has great potential to alleviate costly expert delineation labeling. However, due to the lack of precise size and boundary guidance, the effectiveness of PSS often falls short of expectations. Although recent vision foundational models, such as the medical segment anything model (MedSAM), have made significant advancements in bounding-box-prompted segmentation, it is not straightforward to utilize point annotation, and is prone to semantic ambiguity. In this preliminary study, we introduce an iterative framework to facilitate semantic-aware point-supervised MedSAM. Specifically, the semantic box-prompt generator (SBPG) module has the capacity to convert the point input into potential pseudo bounding box suggestions, which are explicitly refined by the prototype-based semantic similarity. This is then succeeded by a prompt-guided spatial refinement (PGSR) module that harnesses the exceptional generalizability of MedSAM to infer the segmentation mask, which also updates the box proposal seed in SBPG. Performance can be progressively improved with adequate iterations. We conducted an evaluation on BraTS2018 for the segmentation of whole brain tumors and demonstrated its superior performance compared to traditional PSS methods and on par with box-supervised methods.

candidates.title: nnU-Net: Breaking the Spell on Successful Medical Image Segmentation.
candidates.abstract:
Fueled by the diversity of datasets, semantic segmentation is a popular
subfield in medical image analysis with a vast number of new methods being
proposed each year. This ever-growing jungle of methodologies, however, becomes
increasingly impenetrable. At the same time, many proposed methods fail to
generalize beyond the experiments they were demonstrated on, thus hampering the
process of developing a segmentation algorithm on a new dataset. Here we
present nnU-Net ('no-new-Net'), a framework that automatically adapts itself to
any given new dataset. While this process was completely human-driven so far,
we make a first attempt to automate necessary adaptations such as
preprocessing, the exact patch size, batch size, and inference settings based
on the properties of a given dataset. Remarkably, nnU-Net strips away the
architectural bells and whistles that are typically proposed in the literature
and relies on just a simple U-Net architecture embedded in a robust training
scheme. Out of the box, nnU-Net achieves state of the art performance on six
well-established segmentation challenges. Source code is available at
https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/nnunet.
